item.title: Execute on a device
item.description:
Run the particle movement kernel on an explicitly selected accelerator, then check the result against an independent host run. Start with systems and kernel access and shared time. Device execution is experimental; use the pinned Mojo/MAX environment and a working supported accelerator.

Define a transferable movement stage

This stage keeps the particle names and uses Float32 arithmetic, including on host, so its arithmetic also compiles for Apple GPUs.

@fieldwise_init
struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic."""

    var x: Float32
    var y: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time."""

    var dx: Float32
    var dy: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Time(Copyable, Movable):
    """Shared simulated step length."""

    var delta: Float32

Position and Velocity declare TrivialRegisterPassable, the component transfer requirement. Time is an ordinary resource: its recursively checked, pointer-free representation qualifies without that trait. A component trait check does not establish resource eligibility, and a host pointer field does not become a device allocation through byte copying.

Declare the readable inputs and writable position before selecting a target.

comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]()
comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]()


def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]):
    """Moves each row using its velocity and the shared step length.

    Args:
        context: Matching rows and read-only time.
    """
    ref time = context.resources.get[Time]()
    for particle in context:
        ref position = particle.get[Position]()
        ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]()
        position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta
        position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta

move reads Velocity and Time and updates Position. The filter controls component matching and access; Resources separately declares resource access. include uploads and downloads the component, read uploads only, and write downloads only. A write-only component supports set, not get; initialize it for every visited row because its previous host bytes are not uploaded.

Select the target in the system

The system specializes SystemContext.run for a ExecutionBackend value.

@fieldwise_init
struct Move[backend: ExecutionBackend](System):
    """Selects the execution target explicitly."""

    def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises:
        """Runs one synchronous movement step.

        Args:
            context: Access to this simulation's world.

        Raises:
            Error: If resource preparation or execution fails.
        """
        context.run[move, backend=Self.backend]()

Move[ExecutionBackend.HOST]() uses sequential host execution, also the default when backend is omitted. Move[ExecutionBackend.DEVICE]() requests a device. The choice is compile-time; a runtime choice needs an explicit branch calling each specialization. The same choice is available on EntitySelection.run for exact selected ranges.

The execution mapping changes how often code outside the entity loop runs.

One row loop, three invocation mappings.

Store A and Store B are physical stores, which can belong to the same logical archetype. Sequential host calls cover stores or exact selected ranges; threaded calls may split those ranges. Device threads divide the packed rows in one launch using grid-stride iteration. Each matched row is visited once; row indices are local to the prepared context, never stable entity IDs.

Account for transfers and completion

By default, every device call uploads all readable columns and resources. The transfer path packs only matching ranges and scatters writable results back to their original host stores.

Access declarations determine transfer directions.

The upload arrows carry both readable columns; the return arrows carry only Position. Gaps outside a selection remain untouched. Resource views and capture values bind separately from these columns. Allocation capacity can persist between calls; skipping unchanged data uploads requires the separate copy-reuse option.

run returns after the launch, synchronization, and writable component, read-write resource, and mutable-capture copy-back finish. The next system sees those host values. Downloads use owned staging and publish after successful synchronization. A transfer or synchronization failure discards unpublished staged outputs and drains the queue; if completion remains unknown, the world rejects further execution. Host effects are not rolled back. An adapter finalizer can raise after publication; its published outputs remain.

Execute and compare independent runs

The checked driver seeds 37 movers and an unmatched marker, runs two steps per target, and checks every coordinate before comparing sums.

def run_stage[backend: ExecutionBackend]() raises -> Position:
    """Runs two steps and checks both coordinates and an unmatched marker.

    Parameters:
        backend: Explicit target for this independent simulation.

    Raises:
        Error: If setup, execution, or a position check fails.

    Returns:
        The sum of the moving particles' final coordinates.
    """
    var world = World[Position, Velocity]()
    world.resources.add(Time(0.25))
    _ = world.storage.add_entities(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 2), count=37)
    var marker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(-3, -3))
    var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity](world^)
    scheduler.add_system(Move[backend]())
    scheduler.run(steps=2)
    var total = Position(0, 0)
    for particle in scheduler.world.storage.query[move_filter]():
        ref position = particle.get[Position]()
        assert_almost_equal(position.x, 0.5)
        assert_almost_equal(position.y, 1.0)
        total.x += position.x
        total.y += position.y
    assert_equal(scheduler.world.storage.read[Position](marker).x, -3)
    return total


def main() raises:
    """Reports device execution separately from a hardware skip.

    Raises:
        Error: If host checks, device execution, or parity checks fail.
    """
    var host = run_stage[ExecutionBackend.HOST]()
    assert_almost_equal(host.x, 18.5)
    assert_almost_equal(host.y, 37.0)
    print("PASS: host particle checks")
    comptime if has_accelerator():
        var device = run_stage[ExecutionBackend.DEVICE]()
        assert_almost_equal(device.x, host.x)
        assert_almost_equal(device.y, host.y)
        print("PASS: actual device execution and host/device parity")
    else:
        # A skip is an application choice; DEVICE itself never falls back.
        var empty = World[Position, Velocity]()
        empty.resources.add(Time(0.25))
        var context = SystemContext(empty)
        with assert_raises():
            context.run[move, backend=ExecutionBackend.DEVICE]()
        print("SKIP: device parity (no accelerator compilation support)")

Each mover ends at (0.5, 1.0) and the marker stays at (-3, -3). The non-block multiple exercises device iteration beyond a trivial single-row launch. has_accelerator() gates this program’s optional validation; it is not a Larecs fallback. Once the program attempts DEVICE, initialization or execution errors propagate. The no-support branch instead checks that even an empty DEVICE request raises.

From the repository root, run the checked source:

pixi run mojo run -I src examples/particles/device.mojo

PASS: actual device execution and host/device parity confirms executed device work. SKIP: device parity ... confirms only the host path; compilation or a hardware skip does not validate the accelerator result.

Troubleshooting and limits

Failure or restriction Response
DEVICE unavailable DEVICE raises even with no matching rows. Fix the accelerator/toolchain or explicitly choose HOST. There is no automatic fallback.
Empty match on a working device Required resources and adapters still validate; no device allocation, upload, or launch occurs. Captures stay unchanged. Mutable adapters still prepare/finalize host output.
Component transfer rejection Use components satisfying the device transfer check; keep owning collections on the host. Only accessed component types are checked.
Ordinary resource rejection Use recursively pointer-free trivial values, or an adapter for an owner. PlainValue is a trusted declaration for opaque pointer-free trivial fields, not permission to transfer pointers.
Resource access rejection Ordinary device resources allow read and read_write, not write. Mutable shared values require race-free writes.
Closure or threaded/device combination rejected Device entry points are thin kernels. Lexical callables require sequential HOST; threaded=True requires HOST.
Missing resource, including on an empty match Add every declared source during setup. Device availability is checked before resource preparation.

Keep expensive work per particle; transfers and preparation can dominate a small kernel. Measure complete simulation steps before choosing a backend.

item.title: Pass local values to kernels
item.description:
Pass a step-local scale or result without storing it as a world resource. Start with movement and resources. Choose a lexical closure for sequential host borrows, or explicit slots for a thin kernel that can also run on a device. Threaded execution accepts neither capture path; its inputs belong in read-only resources or components.

Borrow locals on the host

Both independent programs on this page use these particle types.

@fieldwise_init
struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic."""

    var x: Float32
    var y: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time."""

    var dx: Float32
    var dy: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Time(Copyable, Movable):
    """Shared simulated step length."""

    var delta: Float32

The names match the core simulation. The explicit-capture variant uses the same Float32 representation for device-compatible arithmetic; see device eligibility.

The lexical stage defines move inside Move.update and passes it as a value.

@fieldwise_init
struct Move(System):
    """Counts particles through a sequential host closure."""

    def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises:
        """Moves the particles and observes a synchronous captured result.

        Args:
            context: Access to the particle world.

        Raises:
            Error: If resources, execution, or the visit check fail.
        """
        var scale: Float32 = 2
        var visits = 0

        def move(
            rows: KernelContext[
                Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity](),
                Resources().read[Time](),
            ]
        ) {imm scale, mut visits}:
            """Moves each row and counts it through a host borrow.

            Args:
                rows: One matching physical store's rows and time.
            """
            ref time = rows.resources.get[Time]()
            for particle in rows:
                ref position = particle.get[Position]()
                ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]()
                position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta * scale
                position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta * scale
                visits += 1

        context.run(move)
        assert_equal(visits, 2)

imm scale borrows the local input and mut visits borrows the counter. context.run(move) selects the value-taking overload, which supports only sequential HOST. Every matching physical store receives a call, so visits increments inside the row loop. Completion is synchronous; its final value is visible at the assertion. Do not capture an alias that structurally changes the world while rows are borrowed.

The driver checks two matching physical stores with different compositions.

def main() raises:
    """Checks the closure across two matching physical stores.

    Raises:
        Error: If setup, execution, or a position check fails.
    """
    var world = World[Position, Velocity, Int32]()
    world.resources.add(Time(0.25))
    var walker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 0))
    var climber = world.storage.add_entity(
        Position(5, 0), Velocity(0, 2), Int32(1)
    )
    var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity, Int32](world^)
    scheduler.add_system(Move())
    scheduler.run(steps=1)
    assert_almost_equal(scheduler.world.storage.read[Position](walker).x, 0.5)
    assert_almost_equal(scheduler.world.storage.read[Position](climber).y, 1.0)
    print("PASS: lexical host captures across two stores")

walker and climber both move once, and the counter counts rows across both calls. The extra Int32 component puts climber in another logical archetype; it does not change the movement filter. Run pixi run mojo run -I src examples/particles/lexical_closure.mojo from the repository root to check the stage.

Declare explicit slots for a thin kernel

The alternative stage declares ordered Captures slots, independent of the world’s resource types.

comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]()
comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]()
comptime locals_spec = Captures[ReadCapture[Float32], MutCapture[Int32]]()


def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources, locals_spec]):
    """Moves particles and records the processed count with a single writer.

    Args:
        context: Rows, time, and ordered scale/count capture slots.
    """
    ref time = context.resources.get[Time]()
    var scale = context.captures.get[0]()
    for particle in context:
        ref position = particle.get[Position]()
        ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]()
        position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta * scale
        position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta * scale
    # The count is shared, not one private scalar per device thread.
    comptime if is_gpu():
        if global_idx.x != 0:
            return
    context.captures.get[1]() += context.length

Slot 0 is a ReadCapture input; slot 1 is a MutCapture result. get[0] is immutable. The output is shared by all invocations/threads, not private per row. On host, one writer per store adds that store’s length. On device, only global thread zero adds the packed length, after its own row loop. This works because the result does not read other threads’ outputs. It is not a barrier or a general parallel reduction.

Bind locals in exactly the declared order when the system runs.

@fieldwise_init
struct Move[backend: ExecutionBackend](System):
    """Binds local values for one synchronous step."""

    def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises:
        """Checks count copy-back before the system returns.

        Args:
            context: Access to the simulation world.

        Raises:
            Error: If binding, execution, or the count check fails.
        """
        var scale: Float32 = 2
        var processed: Int32 = 0
        context.run[move, backend=Self.backend](
            read_capture(scale), mut_capture(processed)
        )
        assert_equal(scale, 2)
        assert_equal(processed, 37)

read_capture and mut_capture borrow their locals until run finishes. Host execution borrows the original values; device execution uploads each binding on every call and copies mutable slots back before return. Empty matches leave captures unchanged. The checked full program also tests an empty world and 37 particles split across two physical stores.

From the repository root, execute this independent stage:

pixi run mojo run -I src examples/particles/captures.mojo

The program always checks host execution. Its explicit device PASS line means actual execution and copy-back; a SKIP line means that device validation did not run. Device setup explains availability failures.

Restrictions and recovery

Failure or restriction Response
Wrong slot count, type, or mutability Match Captures in binding order. Slots may share a type; their index still distinguishes them.
Conflicting borrows of one local Use separate values; the borrow checker rejects overlapping read/mutable bindings.
Heap owner or host pointer in a device capture Captures transfer trivial bytes, not object graphs, and perform no DevicePassable conversion. Use a portable resource for owned storage.
A captured reference outlives execution Keep references and pointers inside the invocation. Neither lexical nor explicit capture references may escape it.
Several writers update one output Choose a proven single writer or per-row output and a later reduction. Mutable capture access supplies no synchronization.

Device execution remains experimental. Prefer explicit bindings when the same thin kernel must run on both targets; use portable resources when the input persists between steps or owns data.

item.title: Use portable resources
item.description:
Read an owning sample collection through the same particle kernel on host and device. Start with shared resources and device selection. Adapter-backed device execution and mutable adapters follow the experimental status. This stage uses read-only views; kernel outputs remain per-entity components.

Separate the owner from the kernel view

The particle fields stay plain; time remains an ordinary read resource.

@fieldwise_init
struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic."""

    var x: Float32
    var y: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time."""

    var dx: Float32
    var dy: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Time(Copyable, Movable):
    """Shared simulated step length."""

    var delta: Float32

These types have no heap ownership. The new resource sources below instead own collections and expose a different representation inside kernels.

Use BufferResource for a contiguous scalar buffer. Add a custom DevicePassableResource only when the kernel needs a domain-specific view, such as the last sample of a rectangular grid.

comptime Samples = BufferResource[DType.float32]


@fieldwise_init
struct Grid(DevicePassableResource):
    """Owns samples and dimensions on the host."""

    comptime Adapter = GridAdapter
    var values: List[Float32]
    var width: Int
    var height: Int


@fieldwise_init
struct GridView(TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Borrows immutable samples in the current target's address space."""

    var values: Pointer[Float32, ImmUntrackedOrigin]
    var width: Int
    var height: Int

Implement validation and target preparation

Larecs validates sources, leases them, and retains descriptors until synchronous completion, including the join of threaded host workers. item.title: Run threaded host kernels
item.description:
Run independent particle rows in concurrent host chunks, then compare their results with sequential execution. Start with systems and kernel access. Threading is experimental; it changes invocation boundaries within one kernel call, while systems still run in registration order.

Keep inputs portable and work independent

The stage uses plain components and explicitly read-only time.

@fieldwise_init
struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic."""

    var x: Float32
    var y: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time."""

    var dx: Float32
    var dy: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Time(Copyable, Movable):
    """Shared simulated step length."""

    var delta: Float32

The component fields contain only scalar values. Threaded eligibility checks pointer-free trivial representation for accessed components; a device component trait alone does not establish this. Unaccessed owning components can coexist in the world.

The movement loop changes only its own row.

comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]()
comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]()


def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]):
    """Moves each row using its velocity and the shared step length.

    Args:
        context: Matching rows and read-only time.
    """
    ref time = context.resources.get[Time]()
    for particle in context:
        ref position = particle.get[Position]()
        ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]()
        position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta
        position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta

Resources().read[Time]() shares one immutable time value with every chunk. Ordinary mutable resources, including the Resources[Time]() read-write default, are rejected even when a configuration uses sequential fallback. Adapter views can expose owning read inputs.

Opt in per invocation; configuring the world alone does not enable threading.

@fieldwise_init
struct Move[threaded: Bool](System):
    """Opts into host chunks for this movement kernel."""

    def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises:
        """Moves disjoint rows and joins before returning.

        Args:
            context: Access to the simulation world.

        Raises:
            Error: If threaded eligibility or preparation fails.
        """
        context.run[move, threaded=Self.threaded]()

context.run[move, threaded=True]() requires a nonraising thin kernel and HOST. Lexical closures, explicit captures, and threaded=True with DEVICE fail at compile time. EntitySelection.run supports the same threaded engine on exact selected ranges.

Configure and check the result

This driver compares ordinary sequential execution, one-worker fallback, and a four-task configuration, each from a fresh world.

def run_stage[threaded: Bool](workers: Int) raises -> Position:
    """Checks parallel dispatch and whole-range fallback against exact values.

    Parameters:
        threaded: Whether to opt into the threaded engine.

    Args:
        workers: Submitted task budget; one exercises sequential fallback.

    Raises:
        Error: If configuration, execution, or a result check fails.

    Returns:
        Coordinate sums after two steps.
    """
    var world = World[Position, Velocity](
        execution_config=ThreadedExecutionConfig(
            workers=workers, chunks_per_worker=2, min_parallel_rows=0
        )
    )
    world.resources.add(Time(0.25))
    _ = world.storage.add_entities(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 2), count=4097)
    var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity](world^)
    scheduler.add_system(Move[threaded]())
    scheduler.run(steps=2)
    var total = Position(0, 0)
    for particle in scheduler.world.storage.query[move_filter]():
        ref position = particle.get[Position]()
        assert_almost_equal(position.x, 0.5)
        assert_almost_equal(position.y, 1.0)
        total.x += position.x
        total.y += position.y
    return total


def main() raises:
    """Compares the sequential, one-worker, and multi-task call paths.

    Raises:
        Error: If an execution path disagrees.
    """
    var sequential = run_stage[False](1)
    var fallback = run_stage[True](1)
    var threaded = run_stage[True](4)
    assert_equal(fallback.x, sequential.x)
    assert_equal(fallback.y, sequential.y)
    assert_equal(threaded.x, sequential.x)
    assert_equal(threaded.y, sequential.y)
    print(
        "PASS: sequential, one-worker fallback, and four-task particle parity"
    )

ThreadedExecutionConfig sets a submitted-task budget, not reserved cores or guaranteed OS thread overlap. min_parallel_rows=0 disables the size cutoff so the four-task case takes the chunk-dispatch path. All 4097 rows must end at (0.5, 1.0); the uneven count also exercises final short chunks. This result check alone does not prove simultaneous worker overlap.

From the repository root, run:

pixi run mojo run -I src examples/particles/threaded.mojo

The PASS line confirms parity for all three call paths. Hardware concurrency claims need separate worker-overlap evidence, such as the repository’s threaded correctness tests.

Respect chunk boundaries and lifetimes

Parallel dispatch splits each physical store or selected range independently. Workers claim disjoint chunks dynamically; invocation order is unspecified. Code outside the row loop runs once per chunk. A row’s idx starts at zero in each host context, including each chunk: do not index a shared global output with it or treat it as an entity ID. KernelContext.thread_count remains one inside a host chunk. Cross-chunk dependencies need a later run after the join.

Default settings are one worker, four target chunks per worker, and a 65,536 matched-row cutoff. One worker or fewer rows than the cutoff preserves whole-range sequential calls, after all threaded eligibility checks. Empty matches invoke no kernel. Worker/chunk counts must be positive, their product representable, and the cutoff nonnegative.

Every explicitly threaded run acquires an extra structural lock, even for fallback and an already locked selection. Lock exhaustion raises before work starts. All fallible preparation precedes row writes, and all workers join before the call returns. Fatal worker/runtime failures offer no rollback.

Keep one coordinating caller for the world. Structural locks and resource leases are not mutexes for external aliases. Do not reenter execution, mutate backing resources, or resize/relocate storage through escaped aliases while workers run; copying, moving, replacing, or destroying an active world aborts. Avoid mutable globals and callees with hidden unsafe mutation.

Troubleshooting

Failure or restriction Fix
Plain-value check fails Remove pointers/ownership from accessed components or ordinary read resources. PlainValue may declare opaque scalar-only StaticTuple/InlineArray fields; the author guarantees the entire representation is pointer-free and trivial.
Mutable ordinary resource rejected Use explicit read, per-row component outputs, or an adapter declaring both mutation capabilities. A mutable adapter’s concurrent-write contract remains your responsibility.
Small workload shows no improvement Measure dispatch overhead and complete steps; adjust the cutoff only after profiling.
Structural lock exhaustion or locked world Release unrelated queries/selections before running or maintaining storage. Empty/exhausted cursors can still own locks.

See the execution mapping, shared-write alternatives, and complete-step measurement.

Enable reuse and invalidate escaped writes

The sequence below enables World.reuse_device_copies, reads without invalidating, and then changes resource and component inputs.

    Raises:

    Returns:

    world.reuse_device_copies(reuse)
    var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity](world^)
    scheduler.add_system(Move[backend]())
    scheduler.initialize()
    scheduler.update(steps=1)  # x = 0.25
    _ = scheduler.world.resources.read[Time]().delta
    _ = scheduler.world.storage.read[Velocity](walker).dx
    scheduler.update(steps=1)  # x = 0.5; read calls preserve reuse
    scheduler.world.resources.get[Time]().delta = 0.5
    scheduler.update(steps=1)  # x = 1.0; get advances the resource revision

    # This pointer survives a later run; subsequent writes bypass tracking.
    var time_ptr = Pointer(to=scheduler.world.resources.get[Time]())
    scheduler.update(steps=1)  # x = 1.5
    time_ptr[].delta = 1.0
    scheduler.world.resources.invalidate_device[Time]()
    scheduler.update(steps=1)  # x = 2.5; explicit invalidation refreshes Time
    scheduler.world.storage.get[Velocity](walker).dx = 2
    scheduler.update(

    scheduler.finalize()

read and read-only queries preserve reusable copies. get through mutable storage conservatively advances a revision even if you only read it. The pointer obtained before a later run does not trigger tracking when you subsequently write through it. invalidate_device[Time]() after that write forces a refresh. Reacquiring with get after each run is the preferred alternative. Neither invalidation path permits mutation during a live invocation or makes an invalid reference safe.

The data-validity sequence differs from allocation reuse.

Retained capacity does not prove that its contents are current.

The revision labels identify host data states. A current record skips an upload; a changed record requires one. Downloaded outputs become current after successful completion. A revision mismatch does not require discarding a large enough allocation. This also applies to read-only adapted resources: validation and leases still run, but a current copy skips the whole prepare_device hook and reuses its descriptor and samples. Mutable adapters always prepare; explicit captures upload every call.

Data Operations that can invalidate reusable bytes
Resource Add/set, mutable get, and host/threaded/device runs declaring writable access. Removal discards its records.
Component type in a physical store Mutable storage/row access, setters and kernels declaring writes, including exact selected ranges.
All columns affected by placement Structural changes, spatial row permutations, partition transfers and store growth/replacement.
Escaped references or raw pointers Untracked writes require resource-specific invalidate_device[T]() or World.invalidate_device_copies for all copies.

Component reuse also requires the same store incarnation, contiguous row range, packed offset, and revision. Alternating filters or selections can change pack offsets and cause reuploads despite unchanged host values. A world copy starts with independent host owners and empty device records. Disabling reuse clears records; it does not turn completion asynchronous. Failed queued invocations invalidate their touched copies; an unusable world must still be replaced.

item.title: Coordinate shared writes
item.description:
Produce race-free shared results by writing per-particle output first and reducing it after run completes. Start with kernel access and read the execution restrictions before changing targets. Standalone synchronization primitives exist; automatic KernelContext.sync bindings and deferred retries do not.

Write a separate output for each particle

The stage uses the same particle types and shared time.

@fieldwise_init
struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic."""

    var x: Float32
    var y: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time."""

    var dx: Float32
    var dy: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Time(Copyable, Movable):
    """Shared simulated step length."""

    var delta: Float32

A resource or mutable capture would be one shared value for every worker. The additional Displacement below instead belongs to each entity.

Write all output fields before a later step reads them.

@fieldwise_init
struct Displacement(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """A private output for one particle, avoiding a shared kernel counter."""

    var x: Float32
    var y: Float32


comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]().write[
    Displacement
]()
comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]()


def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]):
    """Writes every per-row output before a later single-caller reduction.

    Args:
        context: Particle inputs and set-only displacement output.
    """
    ref time = context.resources.get[Time]()
    for particle in context:
        ref position = particle.get[Position]()
        ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]()
        var dx = velocity.dx * time.delta
        var dy = velocity.dy * time.delta
        position.x += dx
        position.y += dy
        particle.set(Displacement(dx, dy))

The filter grants read-write Position, read-only Velocity, and set-only Displacement. Every visited row initializes its output. The same row-local work can satisfy device/threaded restrictions without a shared increment.

Reduce the completed output on the coordinating host caller.

@fieldwise_init
struct Move(System):
    """Runs row work before a single-caller reduction."""

    def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises:
        """Reduces completed per-row outputs without a shared kernel write.

        Args:
            context: Access to the world after synchronous kernel completion.

        Raises:
            Error: If execution or the reduction check fails.
        """
        context.run[move]()
        var total = Displacement(0, 0)
        for particle in context.world[].storage.query[
            Filter().read[Displacement]()
        ]():
            ref value = particle.get[Displacement]()
            total.x += value.x
            total.y += value.y
        assert_almost_equal(total.x, 9.25)
        assert_almost_equal(total.y, 18.5)

The query starts after synchronous kernel completion. One caller sums all 37 outputs, obtaining (9.25, 18.5); there is no concurrent write to total. For a fully parallel reduction, use disjoint partial-output components and later passes with explicit dependencies. A single designated writer is also valid when it need not read unfinished work from other threads, as in the capture count example. A thread-zero branch alone is not a global barrier.

Use standalone host primitives when you own the storage

This independent check demonstrates atomic scalars and scoped guarded access outside ECS kernels.

def check_primitives() raises:
    """Checks target-local host primitives independently of ECS bindings.

    Raises:
        Error: If an atomic or guard check fails.
    """
    var counter = AtomicValue[UInt32](0)
    var updates = counter.write_view()
    assert_equal(updates.fetch_add(1), UInt32(0))
    var result = updates.compare_exchange(1, 5)
    assert_true(result.exchanged)
    assert_equal(result.observed, UInt32(1))
    updates.store[Ordering.RELEASE](7)
    assert_equal(updates.load[Ordering.ACQUIRE](), UInt32(7))

    var state = Synchronized[UInt32](10)
    var access = state.write_view()
    var attempt = access.try_read()
    assert_true(attempt.is_acquired())
    var reader = attempt^.take()
    assert_equal(reader.value(), UInt32(10))
    assert_false(access.try_write().is_acquired())
    reader^.release()
    var write_attempt = access.try_write()
    assert_true(write_attempt.is_acquired())
    var writer = write_attempt^.take()
    writer.value() += 5
    writer^.release()
    var read_attempt = access.try_read()
    assert_true(read_attempt.is_acquired())
    var after = read_attempt^.take()
    assert_equal(after.value(), UInt32(15))

AtomicValue owns a scalar; AtomicView borrows it. fetch_add returns the old value, and strong compare_exchange returns both success and the observed value. Only UInt32 and Int32 scalars are supported; add/subtract wrap at that width. Read views allow loads only.

Synchronized owns guarded data; SyncView borrows its canonical protection state. Multiple read guards may coexist, while a writer excludes all guards. try_read/try_write make at most one compare-exchange attempt. Test is_acquired before consuming the result with take. A false result means Busy, including a changed state or reader saturation. It is not an automatic wait or a successful skipped update.

References from guard.value() stay within the guard’s lifetime. Owners and guards are noncopyable; copied views share protection identity. Release by scope exit, including error unwinding, or by consuming guard^.release(). Errors do not roll back payload writes. There is no fairness, blocking wait, lock upgrade, or automatic retry: record required unfinished work for a later pass, or skip only if the application permits losing that update.

Match ordering and backend support

Public atomic operations default to relaxed ordering. Loads additionally accept acquire, stores release, and updates acquire, release, or acquire-release. Pass ordering at compile time. Relaxed counters do not publish adjacent ordinary data. Guards use acquire/release internally.

Target Available behavior
CPU, NVIDIA, AMD Full initial scalar/guard operation set, with CPU-wide or whole-device scope. Backend compilation does not establish hardware correctness.
Apple device Relaxed/acquire loads, relaxed/release stores, relaxed add/subtract. Strong CAS, ordered add/subtract, and guards are explicitly rejected.

Device primitives need aligned, initialized device-accessible payload/state that stays alive until completion. Low-level unsafe view constructors do not allocate, transfer, or validate that memory. A canonical unlocked state must protect every overlapping guarded payload. Host/device allocations are separate domains; these primitives do not permit concurrent CPU/GPU access to one allocation.

Do not put an AtomicView or SyncView into an ordinary resource/capture and expect pointer transfer or automatic synchronization binding. Those raw-byte paths reject these views and aggregates containing them. Kernel binding adapters for these standalone owners remain unimplemented. A custom mutable resource adapter may implement a supported atomic protocol over its own target-local buffers; the checked scatter example demonstrates that separate contract.

The driver creates 37 movers, checks the reduction, and checks the standalone host operations.

Structural locks and resource leases protect invocation lifetimes and do not make shared writes race-free.
